deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics and no derivation. It is a printed publisher's leaflet, the 'Inhalts-Anzeige' (table of contents) of the first two volumes of the 'Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins', edited by C. F. Gauss and W. Weber. It is the reverse of the Weidmann subscription invitation dated Leipzig, November 1838; Gauss used the front of that sheet for his handwritten numerical work.

Volume 1 (1836) lists:
- Gauss's Introduction
- Weber on the design of magnetic observatories and their instruments
- Gauss on the procedure for the observation terms (Termine)
- Gauss's extract from three years of daily declination observations at Göttingen
- Weber's small travelling apparatus for measuring terrestrial magnetism in absolute units
- Gauss's explanations of the term-day drawings and observation numbers
- Data plates: declination variations for 17 Aug, 24 Sep and 26 Nov 1836; lithographs of the Göttingen observatory; term-day drawings for 28 Nov 1835 to 26 Nov 1836; figures of the magnetometer

Volume 2 (1837) lists:
- Gauss's new instrument for directly observing changes in the horizontal intensity (the bifilar magnetometer)
- Weber on the setup and use of the bifilar magnetometer
- Weber on the influence of temperature on bar magnetism
- Gauss's instructions for determining the oscillation period of a magnetic needle
- Weber's induction inclinatorium
- Sartorius von Waltershausen's absolute-intensity observations at Waltershausen
- Weber on reducing magnetometer readings to absolute declinations
- Gauss's explanations of the term-day drawings
- Data and plates: intensity changes at Göttingen (29 Jul, 31 Aug, 13 Nov 1837); declination changes for the 1837 term days; figures of the bifilar magnetometer and the induction inclinatorium

The faint mirror-image heading visible on the page is bleed-through from the front side ('Einladung zur Subscription ... Carl Friedrich Gauss und Wilhelm Weber ... Weidmann'sche Buchhandlung'). It is not text on this side. No handwritten calculations by Gauss appear on this side, apart from a few stray marks in the left and lower margins.
